title: SQL Injection in String Interpolation Queries
platform_conditions: Scala 2.13 / Scala 3 on the JVM; applies to JDBC and database-access libraries built over string interpolation
security_mechanism: The s-interpolator performs plain string substitution before the driver sees the text, so s"SELECT * FROM t WHERE id = $id" sends the attacker's quote/syntax as statement structure and the database parses it as SQL. The same hole exists inside database-library interpolators when a raw fragment is spliced in: an s-interpolated sub-expression embedded into an sql"..." query, or string concatenation for identifiers and ORDER BY clauses, bypasses the parameter binding the library would otherwise apply.

source_sink_clues.source: Request parameters, sort/column names, and filter values fed into s-interpolated or concatenated query text.
source_sink_clues.sink: statement.execute / prepareStatement on s-interpolated strings; query interpolators receiving raw string fragments; identifier/ORDER BY concatenation

tracking_guards: Check values are bound through the library's parameter mechanism (placeholders, the sql interpolator's binder, PreparedStatement.setString); check identifiers and sort directions come from a fixed allowlist map keyed by validated client values.
not_candidate_when: The query uses the database library's parameterized interpolator exclusively, interpolated parts come only from server-side allowlist constants, or the query text is entirely static.
public_references: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in SQL Command — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/89.html
OWASP SQL Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet — https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/SQL_Injection_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html
